assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: **partial**; daemon_capability: **incapable**; driver_capability: **ready** → route **frozen**.

## What the row asserts

`ready → working → waiting` entered while a dialog that belongs to NO tool call is on screen, then `waiting → working → ready` after the user answers, then a ≥15s trailing idle that catches a session left pinned at `waiting`. The point is that nothing carries the entry into `waiting` and nothing carries the release back out, because no tool call is open at either edge.

## agent_supports: partial — one of four triggers, and it is in the wrong place

I checked all four triggers the scenario names, against the installed build (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.83.0` — the package renamed from `@mariozechner/…` since pi's older cells were written).

**1. Sandbox or network-access confirmation — ABSENT.** `docs/security.md:31` is a whole section titled "No Built-in Sandbox": *"Pi does not include a built-in sandbox. Built-in tools can read files, write files, edit files, and run shell commands with the permissions of the pi process."* The document's only mention of network restriction (`docs/security.md:50`) is a recommendation to run pi inside a container, not a dialog pi raises.

**2. First-use trust prompt for the workspace — PRESENT. This is the one.** `docs/settings.md:12-14`: *"On interactive startup, pi asks before trusting a project folder that contains project-local settings, resources, or project `.agents/skills` and has no saved decision for the folder or a parent folder in `~/.pi/agent/trust.json`."* Implementation: `dist/core/project-trust.js` — `resolveProjectTrusted()` falls through to `selectProjectTrustOption()`, which `await`s `ctx.ui.select("Trust project folder?\n<cwd>\n\nThis allows pi to load .pi settings and resources, install missing project packages, and execute project extensions.", …)`, rendered by `dist/modes/interactive/components/trust-selector.js`. It genuinely blocks: `dist/main.js:552` awaits it inside `createRuntime`, so nothing proceeds until the user answers. And it belongs to no tool call — `ui.select` in `core/project-trust.js:9` is the **only** `ui.select(` call site in the whole non-vendor bundle.

The row also offers "…or for a configured server" as part of trigger 2. pi has no such form: it has no MCP (below), so there is no server to trust.

**3. Server-driven MCP elicitation — ABSENT.** `README.md:495`: *"**No MCP.** Build CLI tools with READMEs, or build an extension that adds MCP support."* `docs/usage.md:296` repeats it. `/elicit/i` across `docs/`, `README.md` and the whole `dist/` tree returns **0 hits**.

**4. Auto-mode or settings review the product raises before it proceeds — effectively ABSENT.** The only product-raised candidate is the experimental first-time setup: `dist/main.js:484-485` runs `shouldRunFirstTimeSetup()` → `showFirstTimeSetup()`, and `dist/core/experimental.js` gates the whole experimental surface on `PI_EXPERIMENTAL === "1"`. It is (a) opt-in behind an env var and (b) even earlier in startup than the trust prompt. `/settings` and `/trust` are slash commands the *user* invokes, not reviews the product raises.

### Why `partial` and not `yes`

pi has the behaviour class but not in the position this row asserts. The trust prompt fires **before the session exists**: `docs/extensions.md:280-282` puts `project_trust` above `session_start` in the lifecycle, and `dist/main.js:552` calls it inside `createRuntime`. So there is no preceding `working` to leave, and no `send` can elicit it — step 2 of the row's process ("`send` a prompt that makes the agent raise a blocking dialog") has no pi spelling. The one secondary firing point (`docs/extensions.md:354` — the event also runs "when session replacement (for example `/resume`) enters a cwd whose trust has not been resolved in the current process") does land mid-process, but it still precedes the replacement session and still leaves the *outgoing* session sitting at `ready` with nothing written.

### Why not `no`

Because pi does raise a genuine tool-less blocking modal, and recording that as `no` would tell a future re-assessor "all four triggers checked, none exists" — which is false and would suppress a re-look if the transport ever changed.

## daemon_capability: incapable — neither edge reaches any Source irrlicht reads

Judged against the CURRENT sensor set, re-read rather than inherited (the pi adapter grew a hook channel in #1721, after pi's older permission cells were written).

**No transcript.** `agent.go` declares `Source() = agent.FilesUnderRoot{Dir: sessionsDir()}` over `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`. During the trust dialog there is no file there to tail: `dist/core/session-manager.js`'s `_persist` (lines 722-751) refuses to create the file until an assistant message exists in `fileEntries` — it only flips `flushed` and returns. This repo already knows it independently: `replaydata/agents/pi/driver-interactive.sh` carries the comment *"Pi creates its transcript file under PI_SESSIONS_DIR only after the first user message is processed — there's nothing to read at boot."* So the dialog window produces zero bytes under the watched root.

**The decision is written outside the root, and only after the fact.** Saved trust decisions go to `~/.pi/agent/trust.json` (`docs/security.md:18`) — a sibling of `sessions/`, not under it, so `FilesUnderRoot` never sees it. And it is written *after* the answer, so even a widened watch could only ever mark the RELEASE edge, never the ENTRY the row asserts.

**The only session-shaped row that exists is a presession that cannot carry the arc.** `core/cmd/irrlichd/wiring.go:103` gives EVERY adapter a `processlifecycle.Scanner`, so a running `pi` with no transcript yields a `proc-<PID>` pre-session. That row is born `ready` and never goes `working` — it cannot produce `ready → working → waiting`.

**The hook channel cannot carry it, and subscribing would be worse than useless.** `hookinstaller.go:128` sets `installedHookEvents = []string{HookEventAgentSettled}` — one event, turn-end only. `hookinstaller.go:125-127` states the exclusion in as many words: *"project_trust is pi's ONE genuine blocked-on-user prompt and is excluded because it CANNOT be correlated to a session."* `hooks.go`'s package header carries the measurement: `project_trust` fires before a session exists and its context is explicitly a reduced one — `docs/extensions.md:359`, *"ctx has a limited trust context: cwd, mode, hasUI, and select/confirm/input/notify UI helpers"* — with no `sessionManager` and therefore no transcript path, which is the only key this adapter correlates a session on. Live-confirmed by that issue's event walk against pi 0.83.0: `session_start` is the first event carrying a session file at all. Separately, `docs/extensions.md:367` notes that "the first yes/no decision wins and suppresses the built-in trust prompt" — so a monitoring extension that merely *listened* on that event would be in a position to steal the user's trust decision.

That is `incapable`, not `bug`: there is no trace anywhere for the daemon to mis-handle.

## driver_capability: ready

`driver_step_types_from_file replaydata/agents/pi/driver-interactive.sh` reports `exit_clean, interrupt, keys, reset_session, resume, send, session, slash, sleep, start_session, wait_turn`. Answering a `ui.select` needs `keys` + `sleep`, both present. The blocker is transport and dialog position, not tooling — so this must not be recorded as a driver gap.
caveats: VACUOUS-PASS: the phase schema cannot assert 'no tool call is in flight', which is the row's whole point. If a future pi recording of this row ever went green, the likeliest hollow route is that the phases bound to a DIFFERENT waiting episode — pi's transcript-tail prose cue (a trailing '?' in the last assistant text, the only path by which pi reaches waiting today) or SignalOpenToolStalled on a slow write/edit — rather than to a tool-less dialog. Any re-record must confirm from the transcript that no tool_use block was open at the entry edge, because the spec cannot.

LOAD-BEARING ENVIRONMENT PROPERTY (and a recording prerequisite): the trust prompt appears only when ALL of these hold — the cwd contains a trust-requiring resource (.pi/settings.json, .pi/extensions|skills|prompts|themes, .pi/SYSTEM.md or .pi/APPEND_SYSTEM.md, or .agents/skills in the cwd or an ancestor); ~/.pi/agent/trust.json under the ACTIVE PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR has no saved decision for that dir or any parent; defaultProjectTrust is 'ask' (the default); the mode is interactive; and neither --approve/-a nor --no-approve/-na is passed. A bare `.pi` directory does NOT count (docs/security.md:15) — that is the easy way to build a fixture that silently never raises the dialog. Non-interactive modes (-p, --mode json, --mode rpc) never show it (docs/security.md:26).

DRIVER CAVEAT (not a gap): boot_session in replaydata/agents/pi/driver-interactive.sh waits for the literal string 'Ready' in the tmux pane before it starts stepping. The trust dialog holds the screen before the interactive header prints, so that marker never appears and the loop falls through its 60x0.5s = 30s timeout, then proceeds. A `keys` step would still land, but blind — a future recordable version of this row should assert the dialog's own text ('Trust project folder?') in the pane instead of relying on the readiness marker.

TIMING: stalledEditToolThreshold is 30s (core/domain/session/signal_hold.go, raised from 5s in #1130). It is not a rung this row depends on — no tool is open — but it IS the false-positive source named in the vacuous-pass caveat, and any pi recipe that holds a dialog must hold it well past 30s rather than the `sleep 14` several older recipes still use.

The secondary firing point (docs/extensions.md:354 — project_trust also runs when session replacement, e.g. /resume, enters a cwd whose trust is unresolved in the current process) is the closest pi comes to a mid-session tool-less dialog. It still does not produce the arc: the outgoing session's transcript gets no lines while the dialog is up, so irrlicht shows it at `ready` throughout, and the incoming session does not exist yet.

PROVISIONAL BOUNDARY: this is a docs+bundle+adapter-source read of the installed 0.83.0 build; no recording was run and no model call was made. The agent-layer half (the dialog exists, and where it fires) is settled from source. The daemon half rests on pi writing nothing under ~/.pi/agent/sessions/ during the dialog — read from dist/core/session-manager.js:722-751 and corroborated by this repo's own pi driver comment, but not watched live in this pass.

sources.note: TRIGGER 2, PRESENT: 'On interactive startup, pi asks before trusting a project folder that contains project-local settings, resources, or project .agents/skills and has no saved decision for the folder or a parent folder in ~/.pi/agent/trust.json.' Also the preconditions (a bare .pi directory does not count; non-interactive modes -p/--mode json/--mode rpc never prompt) and the fact that decisions are saved to ~/.pi/agent/trust.json — outside the sessions/ tree irrlicht watches.

The dialog itself: selectProjectTrustOption awaits ctx.ui.select('Trust project folder?…'), rendered by TrustSelectorComponent, awaited inside createRuntime at main.js:552 — so it genuinely blocks. core/project-trust.js:9 is the ONLY ui.select( call site in the entire non-vendor dist bundle, which is what makes this pi's single tool-less blocking dialog.

POSITION (why partial, not yes): project_trust sits ABOVE session_start in the lifecycle — 'before project resources load' — so no send can elicit it and no session exists yet. :354 adds the secondary firing point (session replacement into an unresolved cwd). :359 is the structural block on the daemon side: 'ctx has a limited trust context: cwd, mode, hasUI, and select/confirm/input/notify UI helpers' — no sessionManager, therefore no transcript path. :367 'the first yes/no decision wins and suppresses the built-in trust prompt' — a listening extension could steal the user's decision.

TRIGGER 1, ABSENT: 'Pi does not include a built-in sandbox. Built-in tools can read files, write files, edit files, and run shell commands with the permissions of the pi process.' The only network mention (:50) is a containerization recommendation, not a dialog.

TRIGGER 3, ABSENT: 'No MCP. Build CLI tools with READMEs, or build an extension that adds MCP support.' Corroborated by scan: /elicit/i across docs/, README.md and the whole dist/ tree = 0 hits — no MCP means no server-driven elicitation and no configured-server trust prompt.

TRIGGER 4, effectively ABSENT: the only product-raised review is the first-time setup (shouldRunFirstTimeSetup → showFirstTimeSetup), gated on PI_EXPERIMENTAL === '1' and running even earlier in startup than trust resolution. /settings and /trust are user-invoked slash commands, not product-raised reviews.

THE DAEMON PILLAR'S LOAD-BEARING FACT: the session .jsonl is not created until an assistant message exists in fileEntries — until then _persist only flips `flushed` and returns. So during the trust dialog there is no file under ~/.pi/agent/sessions/ for FilesUnderRoot to tail at all.

Independent in-repo corroboration of the same fact: 'Pi creates its transcript file under PI_SESSIONS_DIR only after the first user message is processed — there's nothing to read at boot.' The boot_session loop's readiness marker ('Ready' in the pane) is also what the trust dialog holds back, grounding the driver caveat.

CURRENT sensor set (#1721), re-read not inherited: installedHookEvents = [agent_settled], one event, turn-end only. hookinstaller.go:125-127 — 'project_trust is pi's ONE genuine blocked-on-user prompt and is excluded because it CANNOT be correlated to a session'. hooks.go's header carries the measurement (reduced trust ctx, no sessionManager, no transcript path; session_start is the first event carrying a session file) and concludes pi is a two-state adapter through hooks.

Why even the presession row cannot carry the arc: every adapter (pi included) gets a processlifecycle.Scanner, so a running pi with no transcript yields a proc-<PID> pre-session — born ready, never working, so it cannot produce ready→working→waiting.

driver=ready: step types are exit_clean, interrupt, keys, reset_session, resume, send, session, slash, sleep, start_session, wait_turn. Answering a ui.select needs keys + sleep, both present — the blocker is transport, not tooling.

recipe.notes: FROZEN on the DAEMON axis (daemon_capability: incapable), and separately unreachable in the position this row asserts (agent_supports: partial). applicable:false with no script — the same shape as the mistral-vibe/2-27 and codex/2-27 siblings — because no step sequence can produce the assertion: pi's one tool-less blocking dialog fires from createRuntime (dist/main.js:552) BEFORE session_start, so there is no `send` that raises it and no session to move ready→working→waiting; and while it is up pi has written nothing under ~/.pi/agent/sessions/ (dist/core/session-manager.js:722-751), so neither edge of the episode reaches any Source irrlicht reads. WHAT THE RECIPE WOULD BE if pi ever emitted a correlatable signal for it: prepare a fresh cwd containing a real trust-requiring resource (a .pi/settings.json with actual content — a BARE .pi directory does not count, docs/security.md:15) under a PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR whose trust.json has no decision for that dir or any parent and whose settings leave defaultProjectTrust at 'ask'; launch pi interactively in that cwd with NO --approve/-a; do NOT wait on the driver's 'Ready' marker (the dialog holds it back — poll the pane for the literal 'Trust project folder?' instead); hold the dialog >30s; answer it with `keys` (Enter on a trust option); then send one ordinary prompt, `wait_turn`, and hold a >=15s trailing idle. A re-record must confirm from the transcript that no tool_use block was open at the entry edge — the spec cannot assert that, and pi's trailing-'?' prose cue and SignalOpenToolStalled are both able to mint a waiting episode that would bind the phases while proving nothing.
